approach: Root cause: the scope guard learns why an attempt stopped from free-text closing-reason prefixes kept in two places that disagree (`scope_guard::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` and `disk::is_environment_reason`, which lists only LOW_DISK and CHECK_TIMEOUT). A producer that dies on an expired login is closed as "the producer did not complete: ... 401 ...", which reads as a work failure, so it counts as line spend and attempts. The pause file written then is never rechecked. Fix: (1) in `disk.rs`, one classifier `StopCause::of(reason)`, the only place that decides which closing reasons are environment stops, plus one parser `api_error_status(detail)` that recognises only the CLI's API-error form (`[success|error]: [Failed to authenticate. ]API Error: <status> ...`). No word lists. Status 401 means producer login expired; 429 means usage limit. (2) `producer.rs` closes a producer stop with an `environment:` reason built by `disk::producer_stop_reason(detail)`, which uses the same parser; every other detail keeps today's "the producer did not complete: ..." text. The same parser classifies already-stored records, accepting only that exact form. (3) `scope_guard.rs` drops `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`, adds a pure `verdict_of(JobState, Option<&str>)` that `attempt_of` calls, and `line_pause` recomputes the signals from the line's attempts through a helper shared with `try_watch_line`. A stored pause is returned only while the recomputed level is Pause. `status` shows only marks that still hold. Only `Closed(Failed)` states can be environment stops, so a timed-out or rejected job is never excused by its reason text.

decisions.choice: One classifier `StopCause::of(&str)` in disk.rs. `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop` and the guard's `verdict_of` all call it. `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` leaves scope_guard.rs and lives only in disk.rs.
decisions.reason: The fault is two lists that disagree. With one definition, a new environment kind is added once and both the guard and `athena retry` see it. disk.rs already owns the reason texts and `resumable_stop`.

rejected.option: Add the 401 text to `is_environment_reason` and leave the guard's own prefix check
rejected.why: Keeps two lists and fixes one instance.

rejected.option: Add a stored stop-reason field to a record such as the outcome
rejected.why: Needs a record schema and round-trip changes, and old records would lack it. The closing reason already carries the cause.

decisions.choice: Classify API errors only by the CLI's API-error form and its HTTP status, through a single `api_error_status(detail)` in disk.rs. The detail is `<subtype>: <first 300 chars of result text>` (claude.rs `output_from_result`). Accept an optional subtype of exactly `success` or `error` (a non-success result with is_error set, or an empty subtype), then an optional `Failed to authenticate. `, then require the body to start with `API Error: ` followed by digits. 401 gives ProducerAuth and 429 gives UsageLimit. Words such as token, quota, rate limit, oauth or unauthorized are not matched anywhere. The write path (`producer_stop_reason`) and the read path (`StopCause::of` on stored 'the producer did not complete: ' reasons) call the same function.
decisions.reason: A model's last words under `error_max_turns` or `error_during_execution` are free prose and can mention any of those words. Tying the class to the structured API-error marker and its status, and excluding those two subtypes, means a false positive needs the model's text to begin with 'API Error: 401'. A false positive turns off T1/T3/T5 for that attempt, so the rule is kept narrow. One parser keeps stored records and new records on the same rule.

rejected.option: Match loose words such as 'quota', 'rate limit', 'token' or 'unauthorized' anywhere in the detail
rejected.why: They are ordinary words in code work and in model text. The prefix 'the producer did not complete: ' is on every producer failure, so it narrows nothing.

rejected.option: Add an API-error class field to `AgentOutput` and `ResultEvent` and pass it to `producer_stop_reason` (the driver reads the result event)
rejected.why: Better in principle, but `AgentOutput` is built in many places and fakes, and old stored records have no such field, so a text rule is needed for them anyway. The text rule runs on the driver's own detail format, so both paths share one rule. Left for a follow-up and named in open_questions.

rejected.option: Accept 403, error type names such as authentication_error or rate_limit_error, or any 4xx
rejected.why: Not seen in the repository. Only 401 and 429 are the stops named in the introspections, and each added form widens the false-positive surface.

decisions.choice: The state gate stays. `verdict_of` and `resumable_stop` give Environment or resumable only for `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Failed)`, as `attempt_of` does today. A timed-out job, whose reason is written by mod.rs `keep_timed_out_work` as 'the producer did not complete: {reason}' and then set to TimedOut, still counts as work. `run/mod.rs` is not edited.
decisions.reason: The timed-out path shares the 'the producer did not complete: ' prefix, so the reason text alone cannot tell the cases apart; the state does. `settle_resume_marks` (mod.rs:594) already requires Failed plus `is_environment_reason`, so it picks up the new classifier unchanged.

rejected.why: A timed-out job whose text happened to carry the API-error form would be excused from line spend.

decisions.choice: Compute the pause on read. `line_pause` recomputes the line's signals from its attempts under the current rule and returns the stored pause only while the recomputed overall level is Pause. The file is not deleted or edited. Recompute only ever invalidates a stored pause; it never creates one. A pause is written only by `try_watch_line` after an attempt.
decisions.reason: This fixes stale pauses after a rule change with no migration; editing pause files is out of scope. Pauses for real repeated rejections still hold, because the recomputed signals reach Pause again.

rejected.option: Delete the pause file when the signals clear
rejected.why: Out of scope and loses the record.

rejected.option: Store a rule version in the pause
rejected.why: Needs a new mark field and a version policy; recomputing needs neither.

decisions.choice: `status` uses `Athena::live_marks`, with these rules. A Pause mark is shown only if the recomputed level is Pause. A Flag mark is shown while the recomputed level is Flag or Pause, with the stored kind (a flag that now computes as Pause stays a flag, because only `try_watch_line` writes a pause and the owner's lift or ask clears it). A mark for a line that has no attempts in the records is shown unchanged, because there is nothing to recompute from and the stored mark is then the only evidence. Such a line also covers `status_lists_flagged_and_paused_lines`, whose marks name lines not in the records.
decisions.reason: The producer must not guess how a flag and a recomputed Pause interact or what an unknown line does; each case has a stated reason.

rejected.option: Hide a mark for a line with no attempts
rejected.why: Would hide the only evidence for it.

rejected.option: Upgrade a stored flag to a pause in status when the recompute says Pause
rejected.why: A pause is a write by the guard after an attempt; status must not invent one.

decisions.choice: Split `attempt_of` so `verdict_of(state, reason)` is a pure function, and move signal evaluation into a helper `line_state` used by `try_watch_line` and `line_pause`.
decisions.reason: Tests drive real closing reasons through the production mapping without building JobRecords, and the write path and read path cannot drift apart, including the p90 forecast from the latest request of the line.

rejected.why: Heavy and brittle; the existing Rig covers the end-to-end path.

Rewrite `is_environment_reason` and `resumable_stop` on top of them. Update the module doc and tests, including the one that named `scope_guard::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`.

steps: disk.rs: add `pub const ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX = "environment:"`, `PRODUCER_AUTH` ("environment: producer login expired") and `USAGE_LIMIT` ("environment: usage limit reached"). Add `fn api_error_status(detail: &str) -> Option<u16>` as described in decision 2. Add `enum StopCause { LowDisk, CheckTimeout, ProducerAuth, UsageLimit, OtherEnvironment, Work }` with `StopCause::of(reason)` and `is_environment()`. `of` checks the `environment:` prefix first (LOW_DISK, CHECK_TIMEOUT, PRODUCER_AUTH, USAGE_LIMIT, else OtherEnvironment). Otherwise, if the reason starts with 'the producer did not complete: ', it applies `api_error_status` to the rest: 401 gives ProducerAuth, 429 gives UsageLimit. Anything else is Work. Add `pub fn producer_stop_reason(detail: &str) -> String`: 401 gives `PRODUCER_AUTH: <detail>`, 429 gives `USAGE_LIMIT: <detail>`, anything else gives 'the producer did not complete: <detail>'. Rewrite `is_environment_reason` as `StopCause::of(reason).is_environment()`. Keep `resumable_stop` gated on `Closed(Failed)`. Update the doc comments and the module doc paragraph on environment stops; the `StopCause` doc states the root cause for an outside reader.

disk.rs tests: replace the `scope_guard::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` assertion. Add tests: one per StopCause kind through real text (`LowDisk::text`, `check_timeout_reason`, `producer_stop_reason`); the older stored form 'the producer did not complete: success: API Error: 401 ... OAuth access token has expired' and the 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401' variant; 429; the negative cases in the risks; `one_classifier_decides_environment_reasons` (`is_environment_reason(r) == StopCause::of(r).is_environment()`, and `resumable_stop` agrees, for each kind); `resumable_stop` true for an expired-login Failed stop and false for 'the producer returned no valid report', an admission refusal, Rejected and Landed, and for `TimedOut` with the same reason text (criterion 5, finding 3).

scope_guard.rs: delete `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`; fix the doc references in `Verdict::Environment` and `attempt_of`. Add `pub(crate) fn verdict_of(state: JobState, reason: Option<&str>) -> Option<Verdict>` (Landed gives Accepted, Rejected gives Rejected, Closed(Failed) gives Environment when `StopCause::of(reason).is_environment()` and Failed otherwise, other Closed gives Failed, non-closed gives None). Make `attempt_of` call it.

scope_guard.rs: add private `line_state(records, requests, line) -> (Vec<AttemptRecord>, f64, Signals)` holding the p90 lookup and `evaluate_before_attempt` now inline in `try_watch_line`, and make `try_watch_line` use it. Change `line_pause` to read the mark and return it only when the recomputed `overall()` is `Level::Pause`. Add `Athena::live_marks(&self, records) -> Vec<LineMark>` applying the rules in decision 5. Rewrite the module doc: pauses are computed, not trusted.

producer.rs: replace the format string at the 'the producer did not complete' failure (line ~203-209) with `crate::disk::producer_stop_reason(&record.detail.clone().unwrap_or_default())`. Leave the timeout branch and other failure texts alone.

scope_guard.rs unit tests (criterion 3): replace `the_environment_prefix_is_the_low_disk_prefix` with a table test over every environment kind. Add the four-attempt expired-login line test using `verdict_of` and `evaluate_before_attempt`, in the old stored form and the new `environment:` form, with a work-failure control and a control whose model text mentions 401/token under `error_max_turns`. Add a test that a TimedOut job whose reason has the producer prefix and API-error form maps to `Verdict::Failed`.

Fix `retry_refuses_paused_line` as described in the risks.

status.rs: change the `list_lines(&self.state)` call (around line 1759) and the `lines` field fill to `self.live_marks(&records)`; check that the 'is paused' next-step lines come from the filtered list.
CHANGELOG.md: add an Unreleased entry naming the root cause and the fix. Do not touch athena.toml, defaults.toml or any workflow.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked`. Grep `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` and `starts_with("environment` under crates/ should show the definition and its one use only in disk.rs.

risks.risk: The API-error rule is too broad, so a real work failure is classed as environment and a runaway line is never paused.
risks.mitigation: Accept only subtype `success` or `error` (never `error_max_turns` or `error_during_execution`), and require the body to start with 'API Error: ' and a 401 or 429 status. Negative tests: model text under `error_max_turns` that mentions '401', 'token', 'rate limit', 'quota' or even starts with 'API Error: 401'; 'success: ' text with those words but no API-error marker; 'API Error: 500'; a compile-error message containing 401; and a verifier rejection.

risks.risk: The rule is too narrow and misses the real expired-login text, so the incident repeats.
risks.mitigation: Both the write path and the read path use the same `api_error_status`, so every new stop is classified the same way it is later read. The open question names what to check in fixtures.

risks.risk: Recomputing in `line_pause` breaks existing tests that write a hand-made pause for a line whose attempts do not reach Pause (for example `retry_refuses_paused_line`, which uses rejections of different criteria).
risks.mitigation: Change those tests to a real pause (script `[Some(0), Some(0)]`, as `t4_pause_via_go_and_ask` does). `status_lists_flagged_and_paused_lines` stays valid because its lines are unknown and keep their marks (stated rule).

risks.risk: `line_pause` uses a different p90 forecast than `try_watch_line`, so a T3 pause could flip.
risks.mitigation: Both call `line_state`, which reads the forecast from the latest request of the line.

risks.risk: A producer stop on auth leaves no resume mark, so `athena retry` might be expected to resume a candidate that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: `resume_seed` with no mark starts from the base. The criterion 5 test checks `resumable_stop`; a Rig test also confirms the settle step spends no mark.

demonstrations.method: Content check of the diff: the doc comment on `StopCause` in disk.rs, the module doc of scope_guard.rs, and the CHANGELOG.md entry.
demonstrations.observes: The diff names the root cause: the stop reason was inferred from free-text closing-reason prefixes held in two disagreeing lists, so an auth-expiry stop counted as line spend; the fix is the shared classifier in disk.rs, used by scope_guard.rs, and the pause computed from attempts.

demonstrations.method: Test plus Grep. `one_classifier_decides_environment_reasons` in disk.rs asserts `is_environment_reason(r) == StopCause::of(r).is_environment()` and that `resumable_stop` agrees, for each kind. A Grep of `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` and `starts_with("environment` under crates/ finds the definition only in disk.rs. `attempt_of` reaches the classifier through `verdict_of`.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes; the Grep shows one definition of which closing reasons are environment stops, and `scope_guard` has no list of its own.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in scope_guard.rs `mod tests`. Test A: for four attempts of 40 minutes and $1.50 each, map the expired-login reason through `verdict_of(JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Failed), Some(reason))`, in the new `environment:` form from `disk::producer_stop_reason` and in the older stored form 'the producer did not complete: success: API Error: 401 ... OAuth access token has expired'. Build `AttemptRecord`s with the existing `att` helper and assert `evaluate_before_attempt(&attempts, 2.0)` gives Level::None for t1, t3 and t5. Controls: 'the producer returned no valid report' on the same attempts gives t1 Flag and t5 Pause, and an `error_max_turns` detail whose text mentions '401' and 'token' gives the same signals as the work failure. Test B: a table over every environment kind (`LowDisk::text`, `check_timeout_reason`, the producer-auth and usage-limit reasons from `disk::producer_stop_reason`) asserts each maps to Verdict::Environment and raises no signal. Test C: a TimedOut state with the producer prefix and API-error form maps to a non-Environment verdict.
demonstrations.observes: The expired-login line raises no signal at t1, t3 or t5; the controls do; every environment kind is Verdict::Environment, not one job's text; a TimedOut job still counts as work.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the classifier change the older 401 text maps to Verdict::Failed; t1 flags at the third attempt and t5 reaches Pause at 120 minutes, so test A fails. The usage-limit and auth rows of test B fail too. Without the state gate, test C fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `scope_guard::verdict_of` (added in step 3) and `evaluate_before_attempt` (exists, read in scope_guard.rs). Input is real closing-reason text built from the production helpers (`LowDisk::text`, `check_timeout_reason`, `disk::producer_stop_reason` added in step 1) and a literal stored-form string. No fake or double; the `att` helper in `mod tests` is listed as existing from the previous plan's reading, and the producer should confirm it before relying on it.

open_questions: The exact detail the driver stores for an expired login is taken from the brief ('401 OAuth access token has expired'), not from a stored record. The CLI's usual form is a result with is_error set and the text 'API Error: 401 ...', possibly with a 'Failed to authenticate.' lead. If the stored text has neither marker, new stops are still classified correctly (the same parser runs at write time) but old stored records stay work; the producer should note it if it finds a real sample in test fixtures.
The usage-limit text is not in the repository. Only 'API Error: 429' is matched. A usage-limit stop in another form stays work until a sample is found.
A follow-up could have the driver pass the API-error class and status from the result event instead of re-parsing the detail; not done here because AgentOutput and its fakes would change.
`TimedOut` producer stops (mod.rs `keep_timed_out_work`) still count as work in the guard. That is a different cause, not listed in the brief, so it is left as is.
